content:
maria-support: FYI — ACME emailed complaining their invoice shows ~2.3x the token usage compared to the usage dashboard for 2024-11-28 to 2024-11-29. They think client retries after timeouts are being billed twice. Can we triage?
jamal-engineering: Ack, sending to eng. Do we have account id + example request ids from the customer?
maria-support: Account: acct_01G5XYZ. They pasted a couple of example request IDs from their app logs: rq_8f3a2 and rq_8f3a2_retry (they show identical payloads). Said retries happened ~15s after first attempt — appears to be client-side retry after gateway timed out waiting on a long S2S call.
olivia-sre: Can you pull ingress logs for that account/time window? I want to see whether the gateway forwarded both attempts to the runtime or the client got a success but resent.
maria-support: On it.
ingress-bot: logs attached (snippet):
```
[2024-11-28T23:12:01Z] acct=acct_01G5XYZ x-request-id=aa1a2a path=/v1/generate status=504 latency=15.02s
[2024-11-28T23:12:16Z] acct=acct_01G5XYZ x-request-id=aa1a2b path=/v1/generate status=200 latency=2.12s downstream-id=rq_8f3a2
[2024-11-28T23:12:16Z] acct=acct_01G5XYZ x-request-id=aa1a2c path=/v1/generate status=200 latency=2.14s downstream-id=rq_8f3a2_retry
```
jamal-engineering: Hmm — first entry is a 504 at the gateway at 23:12:01, then two 200s a few seconds later but with different x-request-id headers. Downstream-id shows both forwarded to runtime with different internal ids. Looks like gateway timed out on the first connection but the runtime still processed the request and also processed the retry. Metering currently charges per runtime request, so both hits got counted.
jamal-engineering: Do we have x-idempotency-key header behavior recorded? If the customer set idempotency keys our gateway should dedupe before metering.
ingress-bot: No idempotency-key present in these entries. Payloads are identical but client didn't set idempotency-key.
devon-billing: That would explain the doubled token count. But ACME said dashboard shows lower usage — any idea why dashboard differs from invoice?
jamal-engineering: Dashboard is driven by aggregated request meta from the gateway which currently dedupes some retry cases when the gateway returns a 504 quickly and we never saw the downstream success in the same connection. Invoice is generated from the metering ledger which records runtime accept events. In this flow: gateway timed out (logged as 504), client retried, runtime processed both requests -> ledger recorded two consumptions but dashboard aggregated the first attempt as a failure (not counted), so invoice > dashboard.
maria-support: Customer understandably upset. What's the recommended short-term mitigation we can offer?\olivia-sre: Short-term: ask ACME to add an Idempotency-Key header to their calls (and keep it consistent across retries). That will let gateway dedupe on retries. Also recommend increasing gateway timeout to avoid premature client retries if their workloads have long tail latency.
jamal-engineering: I'll open a patch request to add a dedupe-before-metering rule: if the incoming request has an Idempotency-Key header, the gateway will return the previously cached response and will not forward duplicate to runtime; and ensure metering only counts forward events. Long-term we should also correlate connection-level timeouts vs downstream completions and mark those gateway-timeout + downstream-success pairs for ledger reconciliation.
devon-billing: For ACME's billing: I'll open a billing adjustment request and mark it as "under investigation". Need exact runtime request ids and token counts to compute credit. @jamal-engineering can you grab the runtime request ids and token deltas for acct_01G5XYZ 2024-11-28T23:12:00-23:20:00?
jamal-engineering: On it — pulling runtime logs now.
ningress-bot: runtime logs snippet:
```
[2024-11-28T23:12:02Z] runtime-id=r_993 downstream-id=rq_8f3a2 tokens_in=18 tokens_out=332 status=completed
[2024-11-28T23:12:16Z] runtime-id=r_994 downstream-id=rq_8f3a2_retry tokens_in=18 tokens_out=332 status=completed
```
jamal-engineering: Two completed runtime entries with identical token usage; ledger will have two entries. I'll dump full request ids and send to billing in a secure ticket.
maria-support: Provided ACME with suggested short-term fixes and told them billing team will follow up. They asked for a reproduction they can test — can we give them a curl example showing how idempotency-key helps?
olivia-sre: Example curl to reproduce client-side retry flow (simulate timeout then retry):
```
# simulate long-running request + client retry
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"long tail","max_tokens":300}' --max-time 10 || true
# retry WITH idempotency key
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: cust-test-20241128" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"long tail","max_tokens":300}'
```
jamal-engineering: Note: if they reuse the same Idempotency-Key across retries, gateway will dedupe and return the cached response. If the first attempt succeeded downstream but gateway timed out, the second request will be served from cache and not recharged.
devon-billing: Billing ticket created: BT-2024-4819. Assigned to billing ops for provisional credit calculation. Will wait for jamal's dump of ledger ids.
jamal-engineering: Pushed ledger ids to internal ticket and flagged a follow-up to add a reconciler job that marks gateway-timeout + downstream-success duplicates for review.
maria-support: Thanks all. ACME wants estimated timeline for a permanent fix — can eng give ETA?
jamal-engineering: Short-term dedupe-with-idempotency header: docs + gateway config can go out in 3 business days. Reconciler + ledger-side dedupe is a couple sprints (4–6 weeks).
olivia-sre: I'll add a monitor to alert when invoice vs dashboard > 1.5x for an account for >1 day. That should catch regressions.
maria-support: Perfect. I'll update ACME and leave ticket open until billing resolves credit and eng ships the config. :thumbsup:
